newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St pulls Euroshares higher, gold sags.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St pulls Euroshares higher, gold sags.

text.p: European shares were pulled higher on Friday when Wall Street opened strongly again after two days of robust gains, one factor behind a slide in gold prices.
"The U.S. market is looking fairly good and that's keeping us healthy," a dealer in London said.
By midafternoon, London's FTSE index of top shares was up 42.2 points, or one percent, at 4,270.6, while in Frankfurt the DAX index closed up 17.83 points, or 0.59 percent, at 3,035.15.
France's CAC 40 index was up 14.81, or 0.59 percent, at 2517.87, after being down slightly at midday.
Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average was up 30.79 points, or 0.45 percent, at 6,854.65, after rallying some 170 points on Wednesday and Thursday following a five-day slide.
But much stronger than expected fourth quarter U.S. gross domestic product figures gave European markets a brief scare when they showed annualised growth of 4.7 percent.

Bonds dipped, dragging London's FTSE in their wake, although markets then rallied as investors focused on two broad inflation measures in the GDP report which suggested the rate of price rises remained generally in check.

The implicit price deflator rose at a 1.4 percent annual rate in the fourth quarter, down from 1.7 percent in the third quarter and a separate fixed-weights measure of price changes slowed to a 1.8 percent rate of increase from two percent in the third.
"The figures seem to have been regarded as good for the market and after a bit of a panic we're on the way up again," a dealer in London said.
Dealers said the firm performance by the Dow prompted London's FTSE's to attack its all-time high of 4,273.4.

But business could remain overshadowed by the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting next week. The Committee sets interest rate policy and some fear it may raise rates to counter the threat of inflation.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
German shares closed bourse trading at a record after the IBIS DAX index set an all-time intraday high in pre-bourse screen trade of 3,050.88 points.
Rising Bunds and the steady dollar coupled with Wall Street's overnight gains to push prices higher.
SAP rose nearly 11 percent after the blue-chip software group shocked the market by beating its own results forecasts for 1996. Porsche also rose 10.5 percent, after announcing strong profits.
In France, Europe's most bullish market on Thursday, shares also rose, after dipping into the red at midday.
The dollar rallied a touch after drifting lower against the mark and yen as the market took a lack of fresh incentives as an opportunity to adjust following the recent rally.

Traders said remarks by German and Japanese officials overnight expressing concerns about the currency market were weighing on the dollar. Support levels were broken on the way down, accelerating its fall against the mark and the yen. The dollar was at 1.6365 marks and 121.25 yen at 1500 gmt.

The pound was also vulnerable after heavy selling against the dollar and yen spilled over into mark trade. There were signs that British interest rates may not rise as soon as expected, traders said. By mid afternoon, the pound stood at around $1.60 and 2.6195 marks. Gold remained weak in the afternoon, although it was fixed at $345.50, compared with $345.00 in the morning, its lowest since September 14, 1993.
The price crumbled overnight, pulling platinum down also, although it rallied a touch on news suggesting that Russian state gold stocks were nearly exhausted.
Gold, which has plunged from about $370 at the start of the year, has also been shunned by investors who prefer to pour money into the booming U.S. stock market.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6365 marks and 121.25 yen, compared with late Thursday's European levels of 1.6382 marks and 121.61 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 42.2 points at 4,270.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 14.81 points at 2,517.87. FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 17.83 points at 3,035.15.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $345.50 compared with $345.00 in the morning, its lowest since September 14, 1993, and down sharply from Thursday's close in Europe of $347.35.
